newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu says time for Arafat meeting -radio.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu says time for Arafat meeting -radio.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called on Wednesday for a meeting with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to conclude negotiations on Israel's handover of most of Hebron to the PLO, Israeli media said.
Israel Radio and Israel's army radio said Netanyahu made the comment to their reporters aboard his plane flying him home to Israel from Ireland.
"Prime Minister Netanyahu said the time has come for him to meet with Arafat because in fact the agreement on Hebron is complete and what is demanded now is the leaders' decision," Israel Radio said.
Army radio said that while Netanyahu called for a meeting, none had as yet been set.

Arafat, who heads the Palestinian Authority in charge of self-rule enclaves set up in most of the Gaza Strip and parts of the West Bank under previous interim peace deals, was in Cairo on Wednesday. He was expected to return to Gaza on Thursday.

For two months, Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) have been negotiating implementation of a deal signed by the PLO and Israel's previous government in which Israel is to hand 80 percent of the West Bank town to PLO rule.
The talks on the long-delayed Hebron deal began on October 6 after Netanyahu and Arafat attended a Washington summit hosted by President Bill Clinton with Jordan's King Hussein.
The summit was called after 60 Palestinians and 15 Israeli soldiers were killed in clashes in September sparked by Israel opening an entrance to a tunnel near Moslem sites in Jerusalem.
The PLO and Israel have accused each other of delaying a deal on implementing the Hebron handover, which should have occurred in March.
